description:
RFC 8620 §5.3 defines PatchObject as a String → JSON map where keys may carry '/'-separated paths into nested fields and a null value removes the leaf. Currently every type crate uses 'serde_json::Value' (or 'serde_json::Map<String, Value>') directly for PatchObject values, with no documentation handle to bind the prose contract to the type system.

A newtype in jmap-types would replace ~30+ untyped serde_json::Value patch-value sites across the workspace with a documented type that self-explains 'this is a JMAP patch, not arbitrary JSON'.

## Proposed shape

```rust
/// A JMAP PatchObject (RFC 8620 §5.3): a String → JSON map where keys
/// may carry '/'-separated paths into nested fields and a null value at
/// a leaf removes that leaf. The inner JSON shape is intentionally
/// unconstrained — patch contents are spec-defined per-method, and the
/// handler interprets the path semantics.
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
#[serde(transparent)]
pub struct PatchObject(pub serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>);
```

Wire format unchanged (#[serde(transparent)]). The type signature documents the contract without constraining the shape.

## Scope

- Add crate-jmap-types/src/patch.rs (or extend wire.rs) with the PatchObject type.
- Re-export from jmap-types::lib.rs.
- Round-trip tests using RFC 8620 §5.3 example shapes (independent oracle).
- Optionally: adopt PatchObject across the type crates and method handlers (separate sub-bead).

## Initial adoption candidates

Sites where serde_json::Value is currently used for what is semantically a PatchObject:
- jmap-types::SetResponse.updated value: HashMap<Id, Option<T>> — this stays T (the typed object), NOT PatchObject; not affected.
- crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs, calendar.rs, participant_identity.rs — update map values are PatchObject. Currently 'serde_json::Value'.
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs, mailbox.rs, etc. — same pattern, also locked crate.
- crate-jmap-*-client/src/methods/*.rs — calendar_set / calendar_event_set / participant_identity_set update args are HashMap<Id, serde_json::Value>; could become HashMap<Id, PatchObject>.
- crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs trait method update_object<O: SetObject>: O::Patch is currently 'type Patch = serde_json::Value' on every SetObject impl in jmap-calendars-types/jmap-mail-types/etc. — could change to 'PatchObject' without behaviour change.

## Approval gate

Adding to jmap-types (locked). Each downstream adoption may also touch locked crates (jmap-mail-server, jmap-mail-types, jmap-chat-types). All require Mark's per-change approval. Decompose into per-crate children once the base type lands.

## Out of scope

- Changing wire format.
- Adding semantic validation of patch keys (path syntax).
- Adopting PatchObject in handler logic (kept as serde_json::Value internally is fine).

## Source material

- RFC 8620 §5.3 'PatchObject' prose
- ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec/references/rfc8620.txt around line 1990
- crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs:267 — current untyped patch-value usage
notes:
Implementation complete 2026-05-08.

Added crate-jmap-types/src/patch.rs (294 LoC, 11 unit tests + 1 doctest):

Public API additions to jmap-types (LOCKED):
- pub mod patch;
- pub struct PatchObject (re-exported at crate root) — newtype wrapping serde_json::Map<String, Value> with #[serde(transparent)] and #[non_exhaustive].
- Constructors: ::new(), ::from_map(map), Default, From<Map<String,Value>>, From<PatchObject> for Map<...>.
- Accessors: ::as_map() / ::as_map_mut() / ::into_inner() / ::is_empty() / ::len().

Design decisions:
1. Inner Map<String, Value> rather than Value — RFC 8620 §5.3 mandates an object on the wire; arrays/scalars/null are not valid PatchObject wire values. Test 'non_object_json_fails_to_deserialize' enforces this.
2. #[non_exhaustive] + private inner field + explicit constructors — matches the Id/UTCDate/State pattern already used in this crate. Reserves SemVer freedom to add fields later (e.g. metadata).
3. #[serde(transparent)] — guarantees byte-identical wire format to a bare JSON object. The test 'wire_format_is_transparent_json_object' will catch any future refactor that drops the attribute.
4. No path-syntax validation — the wire-format type is path-agnostic; per-method handlers know the target schema and emit invalidPatch errors per RFC 8620 §5.3.

Test oracles (all independent, hand-written from RFC 8620 §5.3):
- empty patch round-trips as {}
- whole-object form (RFC line 1937-1941: 'an entire Foo object is also a valid PatchObject')
- null-leaf removal (RFC line 1925-1927)
- multi-segment JSON Pointer key (RFC line 1918-1920: 'alerts/abc/offset')
- nested object value (RFC line 1929-1930)
- transparent wire format (negative test: must equal Map serialization)
- From/Into Map round-trip
- Default == ::new()
- as_map_mut in-place edits visible on serialize
- non-object JSON values fail to deserialize

Quality gates passed:
- cargo build --workspace clean
- cargo test --workspace clean (113 tests in jmap-types: 102 baseline + 11 new)
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings clean
- cargo fmt --all -- --check clean
- RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p jmap-types --no-deps clean

PLAN.md updated to list the new patch.rs module under the module layout section. Other PLAN.md drift (missing methods.rs, query.rs, backend.rs entries) left alone — out of scope for this bead.

Adoption follow-ups filed (depending on this bead):
- JMAP-wrgs: adopt in jmap-calendars-{server,client,types}
- JMAP-6h5s: adopt in jmap-mail-{server,client,types} (LOCKED — explicit approval per change)

Locked-crate compliance: explicit user approval ('do that bead now') was obtained before touching jmap-types. Public API delta: +1 public type 'PatchObject' (and its associated From/Into impls). Zero changes to existing types/fields/derives/serde attrs.
